core.verdict: The core is technically strong — cost/maxAffordable/sell math is exact, load/sanitize survives hostile input, the loop's catch-up and skippedMs handoff work, formatting handles every extreme, and throughput is 30-48k ticks/s — and the headline fault-isolation test passes (throwing effect, unlock and tick handler each disabled after 3 calls with the game continuing). It falls just short of the 8.5 bar because the isolation guarantee has a verified hole: an intermittently-throwing item is never disabled and, together with the unguarded event bus and a duplicate-pushing 200-entry error ring, it evicts every other diagnostic (the real failures vanished from game.errors in my run). Those are two small, precise fixes in safe.js and events.js; add a core test file and the module is a 9.
issues: [medium] src/core/safe.js guard() resets `fails` to 0 on every success, so an intermittent thrower is never disabled: a test upgrade effect that throws on every other call produced 250 errors in 500 ticks with isDisabled()===false. Combined with the 200-entry errors[] ring and one push per repeat, it evicted every other diagnostic — the 8 entries for the two genuinely broken items (3 failures + 'disabled after 3' each) were gone from game.errors after the run, defeating the module's purpose of preserving what broke. → In guard(), track total failures (or failures per N calls) as well as consecutive ones — e.g. `if (fails >= 3 || total >= 10) disable`. In reportError(), dedupe by `module + msg`: if the last matching entry exists, increment `entry.count` and update `tick` instead of pushing, so one noisy source can never evict distinct errors from the ring.

[medium] src/core/events.js emit() catches listener exceptions but never disables the listener, so a throwing 'tick' listener called reportError + console.error 500 times in 500 ticks (10/s forever; a throwing 'frame' listener would be 60/s). Only ui/index.js render() self-guards; save/tools/any future listener does not, and the spam also fills errors[] (issue above). → In on(name, fn), store `guard('events:' + name, fn)` (keep the original fn as a Map key so off() still works), giving listeners the same disable-after-N behavior as registry callbacks.

[low] src/core has no tests while every other module ships a *.test.mjs (balance, buildings, resources, simulation, ui, upgrades). The maxAffordable float-walk-back, fmt tier-carry logic, sanitize coercions and guard disable semantics are exactly the kind of edge-case code that regresses silently. → Add src/core/core.test.mjs covering: maxAffordable at exact/±epsilon money for n=1..60, buildingCost vs loop sum, sell refund ratio, fmt table (0.5, 9.995, 99.95, 999.99, 999999, 1e15, 1e40, negatives, NaN/Inf), loadState with __proto__/deep nesting/wrong types, guard disable-after-3 and listener isolation.

[low] src/core/format.js is inconsistent across the 1000 boundary: below 1000 values >= 10 are floored (10.96 -> '10', 99.99 -> '99', 999.996 -> '999') while >= 1000 rounds up (999,999 -> '1.00M', 1049.6 -> '1.05K'). A player holding $999,999 sees '$1.00M' next to a '$1.00M' cost whose button is disabled. Also fmtMoney(Infinity) returns '$—' while fmt(Infinity) returns '∞'. → Pick one rule and apply it in both branches: floor to the displayed precision everywhere (Cookie Clicker style) by making tierFixed() use a floor-based variant of roundFixed for money, or round below 1000 as well; make fmtMoney delegate Infinity to fmt ('$∞').

[low] src/core/loop.js: stop() does not clear the Node-fallback setInterval (it only exits on the next 100 ms tick), and loop.skippedMs grows unbounded when the save module fails to load (main.js continues with game.modules.save==='failed' and nothing consumes skippedMs). → Keep the interval id in module scope and clearInterval() in stop(); cap skippedMs (e.g. 24 h) or have loop drain it via step() in small batches when no consumer has claimed it within a few seconds.

[low] src/core/registry.js validate() does not check `currency` (any string other than 'legacy' silently becomes money), `tier` (non-number), or `category`, so a typo like currency:'Legacy' in upgrades/data.js would price a charter perk in money with no registry error. → Add to validate(): `if (def.currency !== undefined && !['money','legacy'].includes(def.currency)) throw`, and `Number.isInteger(def.tier)` / `typeof def.category === 'string'` checks.

balance.verdict: Solid, deeply documented tuning with a top-tier first hour and a cadence that hits the 31-founding shape, but the late game is under-furnished: tension reads 24% vs the 30% contract, replays sit 10-35 minutes on near-flat income with 0-1 upgrades to buy, the priciest visible rung is 1e4-1e8x cash for most of hours 2-6, and the saver profile breaches both magnitude ceilings. High-severity contract miss caps it below 8.5: score 7, no pass.
issues: [high] Purchase-tension contract fails: cheapest unlocked-unowned money upgrade is 30 s-15 min of income away in only 24% of samples (reachShare 0.238, logs/sim-gauntlet.json metrics; reproduced on current tree), contract >= 30%. Cause is structural in config.upgrades: the 16 late core rungs (megastructures $2.1e9 ... galactic-charter $1.2e15) are placed one per city, so during the 10-35 minute plateau of every replay the cheapest unowned upgrade is the NEXT city's rung at >50x cash (hopeless), while everything else is instant. → Add repeatable in-cycle content in config.upgrades: a money-priced 'Municipal Bonds' ladder whose cost = max(1e6, 240 s of current income) x1.5 per purchase, +4% income each, up to ~8 per city and reset on founding. That puts a 4-10 minute target on the card for the whole plateau without moving the cycle table. Re-run npm run sim -- --ticks 432000 and require reachShare >= 0.30.

[high] Dead late-game plateaus vs the Cookie Clicker bar. From the per-city sample table: cities 8-28 gain 0-1 upgrades after minute 3 of the replay and spend 10-35 minutes at <1%/min income growth (city 17: 35 min, 0 new upgrades, 25 flat minutes; city 18: 44.5 min, 1 upgrade, 34 flat minutes; city 28: 41.6 min, 35 flat minutes). Income over the plateau grows only x1.16-1.4 while the player buys ~200 buildings each adding <0.5%. That is a 30-45 minute wait for the Found button in hours 4-8 and 10-11. → Same bond ladder as above plus building-count milestones per type (25/50/100 owned -> +5% income each, config.milestones) so the 200 building buys per cycle carry visible steps. For city 18 specifically, price quantum-exchange 5.2e11 -> 3.5e11 so the x2.8 rung lands in the first half of city 18 instead of lifting only city 19.

[medium] The visible 'next big thing' is hopeless from minute 28 on. config.upgrades prices core rungs at 1e9-1e14 while src/upgrades/data.js still unlocks them on building/pop counts: megastructures ($2.1e9, unlock 3 arcologies) appears at 28 min of city 1 when cash is $1.2e5 and income $28k/s (17,900x cash, 21 h of income); arcology-gardens ($7.6e12) at 32 min; superconductor-grid ($9.1e13) at 35 min = 5e8x cash. Sample bigRatio stays 4e3-6e5 through hours 2-6 (7 h to 14 days of income). Contract text calls this 'hopeless'; Cookie Clicker keeps the priciest visible item at 3-50x. → Give every late core rung an earnings gate like the frontier: in config.upgrades add unlockAt: { earned: cost/4 } (or an earnedGate: 0.25 field consumed by the same applyOverride -> frontierUnlock path), so a rung shows up when the run has earned a quarter of its price. Keep the count/pop rule as an AND if the flavour matters.

[medium] Saver profile breaches both magnitude ceilings: npm run sim -- --saver --ticks 432000 reports money peak 1.96e18 (> 1e18) and legacy 1,459,373 (> 1e6), 37 foundings, 13 empty late cycles (logs/sim-saver.json, reproduced). DESIGN.md: 'both profiles must stay free of overflow/stall/magnitude issues'. → Retune with both profiles in the loop: prestige.exponent 0.488 -> ~0.47 (legacy at 12 h drops ~35%) with firstBonus nudged up (~0.26-0.27) so the default profile's 30th founding stays in hour 12; add two charter perks above Imperial (2e5, 5e5 legacy) as sinks so a saver's surplus has a target. Gate contractPass on the saver run's magnitude issue as well.

[low] Cadence ratio misses: cycle 7 (9.7 -> 13.57 min, x1.40), cycle 9 (16.53 -> 22.4, x1.36) and cycle 28 (30.6 -> 41.57, x1.36) exceed the contract's 'each cycle <= 1.35x the previous'. They pass only because tools/economy-sim.mjs:185 adds +0.5 min slack that the DESIGN.md contract text does not grant. → Either write the +0.5 min slack into DESIGN.md's cadence line, or strengthen the rungs entering those cities: Standing Orders (city 7) gets +10% income, and charter-energy (city 28, no replay income effect) gets a +15% income clause so the Energy Charter city is not the x1.36 step.

[low] Civic 'matters' only by the letter: all 19 happiness dips are the replay's first-minute spree (cycles[].minHappiness 0.36/0.51 in the opening seconds, happiness 2.1-2.8 thereafter); no mature city ever dips, so parks/schools never bind after city 1. → Raise happiness.pollutionScale 0.35 -> 0.45 or let the legacy clean-air tiers scale slower, so a refinery-heavy replay drifts under 1.0 mid-city unless civic buildings keep coming; verify happinessDipCities stays >= 50% and the dips occur after runMin 3.

resources.verdict: PASS. src/resources/ is a clean, pure, allocation-free derived-rate core whose math matches DESIGN.md (with config.js overrides) to the last digit on hand-computed cases, survives pop 0 / demand 0 / 1e300 / NaN / null inputs without throwing or leaking Infinity, and runs at ~1.2 us per call. Zero errors attributable to the module in gauntlet or sim; the sim's only contract failure (tension share 24%) is a balance/pacing matter, not a resources formula defect. Held back from 9+ only by nits: a stale-mods edge in derived.mods, a slightly redundant derived.extra layout with no happiness breakdown for the UI to show, and DESIGN.md math drift versus the saturating pollution curve.
issues: [low] src/resources/index.js line ~288: `derived.mods = m === NEUTRAL_MODS ? derived.mods : m;` - when a caller passes null mods the previous tick's mods object is left in derived.mods (stale) instead of the neutral bag, so derived.mods can disagree with the numbers just computed. → Write `derived.mods = m;` unconditionally (NEUTRAL_MODS is frozen and safe to expose), or document why stale is intended.

[low] derived.extra shape is slightly muddled for UI consumers: `x.pollution` and `x.penalties.pollution` carry the identical value, `x.civic` (the positive term) lives outside `penalties`, and there is no single object that explains the happiness number the way `incomeBreakdown` explains income. Result: src/ui/hero.js reads only `incomeBreakdown` and `unemployment`; no happiness breakdown is shown anywhere, while top-tier idle games always show why a multiplier is what it is. → Add `x.happinessBreakdown = { base: 1, civic, mods: modHappiness, unemployment: -penUnemployment, overcrowd: -penOvercrowd, brownout: -penBrownout, pollution: -pollution, raw, clamped: happiness }` (reused object, same pattern as incomeBreakdown), drop the duplicate top-level `x.pollution`, and have the UI render it as a tooltip on the Happiness tile.

[low] docs/DESIGN.md Resources math is stale versus the code: it still describes pollution as a linear subtraction (code saturates via pollutionCap/pollutionCurve), omits the OVERCROWD_MAX=10 cap and the mods.growth/mods.inflow scaling of popGrowth, and lists derived.extra without pollutionRaw/happinessMult/vacancy/openJobs/powerSurplus. → Update the '## Resources' math block in docs/DESIGN.md to the saturating form `pollution = cap*(1-exp(-x/curve))`, note overcrowd clamp [0,10], the growth/inflow mods, and the full derived.extra field list.

[info] resourceValue('happiness') defaults to 1 when derived.happiness is missing while every other resource defaults to 0; harmless but asymmetric, and the `format: 'power'` path prints `fmt(value) + ' MW'` rather than using the `unit` field declared on the resource. → Use `r.unit` in formatResource (`fmt(value) + ' ' + (r.unit || '')`) so the metadata is the single source of truth.

buildings.verdict: A well-built, error-free catalogue with genuinely good flavor text, four real signature mechanics, clean defensive code and solid tests; every building earns its purchase and tiers stay balanced across 31 prestige cycles. It falls just short of the 8.5 bar on cadence polish: two tier-4 buildings unlock in the same tick at pop 8,000 after a 5.4-minute dead stretch, the arcology and financial district glow unaffordable for 6–7 minutes, the stadium is never bought in the first city, and the module's own header comments quote numbers config.js has since overridden. All fixes are number-tuning in config.buildings plus a comment rewrite; re-run the sim and this passes.
issues: [medium] Double unlock at pop 8,000: src/balance/config.js sets both `techpark` and `nuclear` to popUnlock(8000) (data.js had nuclear at 10,000), so both tier-4 cards appear in the same tick (27.1 min), right after the longest dead stretch of the first city (hospital 21.7 → nothing new until 27.1 min). Mall (3,000) and solar (3,200) also land 12 s apart at 16.4/16.6 min. → In config.buildings set `nuclear: popUnlock(6000, '6,000')` (lands ~24–25 min, filling the gap) and keep techpark at 8,000; move solar to popUnlock(3800) so it follows the mall by ~1.5 min. Re-run tools/economy-sim.mjs and confirm no two buildings unlock within 60 s of each other.

[medium] Stadium is never bought in the first city: it unlocks at 34.9 min (pop 22,000) but at $3.5M base cost the bot first buys it in city 2 (logs/sim-gauntlet.json cycles[1].newItems includes 'stadium'). The tier-4 civic trophy — the only building with 0.25 happiness and 'Eighty thousand voices' flavor — is a glowing, unaffordable card for the last 7 minutes of a 41.5-minute first run. → Lower `stadium.baseCost` in config.buildings from 3.5e6 to ~1.5e6 (the bot holds ~$1M+ by 36 min at 87k–785k/s income) or move its unlock to popUnlock(18000) so it lands ~32 min with ~9 min to afford it; verify the buildings test's tier-4 income-per-dollar band still holds.

[medium] Arcology glows unaffordable for 7.4 min (unlock 19.4 min at pop 4,000, first buy 26.9 min), and financial for 5.6 min — both nearly double the '~4 minutes' target stated in data.js's own 'Unlock spacing' comment. → Either drop `arcology.baseCost` in config from 120000 to ~80000, or raise its gate to popUnlock(5000) (data.js's original) so it unlocks ~22 min and is bought within ~4 min; for financial trim baseCost 7e5 → 5e5 or gate at 14,000.

[low] Windmill gate `powerDemand > 0` guarantees the first cottage is bought into a dark grid: every city's first tick reads powerRatio at the 0.6 floor with a −0.24 happiness brownout penalty (config.js documents this; happinessDipCities=19 of 31). The player sees a brownout before the Power tab even exists. → Make the windmill available from the start (`unlock: null`, unlockHint 'Available from the start') and gate the Power *panel* on demand > 0 instead, or seed one free windmill per city via simulation's fresh-state hook; the 'first brownout ~2.3 min' milestone then fires on a real overload rather than tick 0.

[low] Stale documentation inside the module: the header comment in src/buildings/data.js quotes numbers config.js overrides — 'windmill 6 → coal 80 → solar 900 → nuclear 12k' (windmill is 4 MW, growth 2 via config), tier-4 draws 'arcology 2,500 / financial 4,000 / tech campus 4,500 / stadium 1,500 MW' (config triples them to 7,500/12,000/13,500/4,500), nuclear 'pop(10000)' (config 8,000). Same for docs/DESIGN.md's table (flagged there, but the data.js comment claims to be current). → Rewrite the data.js header to describe *shape* only and point at config.buildings for numbers, or regenerate the quoted figures from the resolved definitions (e.g. a `node -e` snippet printing registry.buildings) whenever config changes; add a test asserting the comment's key numbers match resolved defs if you want them to stay literal.

[low] Power ladder lacks role variety: windmill/coal/solar/nuclear/fusion differ only in $/MW, upkeep and a ±happiness nudge; the config comment even admits fusion is 'a trophy rather than the late-game generator'. No power building has a synergy or a second axis the way the arcology (jobs), stadium (income) and tech campus (clean air) do. → Give one plant a signature rule with the existing synergy system, e.g. solar `synergy: { stat: 'powerGen', source: 'building:park', per: 40, cap: 2, text: 'Output +2.5% per City Park (up to ×2)' }`, and let fusion scale with nuclear count (research spillover) so the late Power tab is a choice, not a $/MW sort.

[low] Synergy handler reads `derived.employed` (financial district) from the previous tick because it runs at priority −10 before 'simulate' recomputes derived; on the first tick after load `derived.employed` is 0 so the financial district's income momentarily reads at base. Harmless in play but the build card can show a one-frame lower number after a load. → In applySynergies fall back to `Math.min(state.res.pop, derived.jobs)` when `derived.employed` is undefined, or document the one-tick lag in the index.js header.

[info] Shared contract failure (not a buildings error): tension share 24% < 30% — the next money-priced item is 30 s–15 min of income away too rarely. Building costs are half of that frontier; tier-4 base costs bunching at $120k–$700k then jumping to $3.5M/$4M (stadium/fusion) contribute to the gaps. → Coordinate with balance/upgrades: after the stadium/arcology cost changes above, re-measure `tensionShare` in logs/sim-gauntlet.json and, if still <30%, add a tier-3.5 rung (e.g. a $1.2M 'Transit Hub' civic building at pop 15,000) between the financial district and the stadium.

upgrades.verdict: The upgrades module is engineered to a high standard — 66 well-named, numerically explicit rungs, contract-compliant charter and frontier ladders, clean mods-only effects, self-deriving hints, founding memory, 0 errors, 14/14 tests, every rung bought in the 12 h sim — but it does not pass the game's own late-game contract: purchase tension is 24% against the 30% target because after the first city each replay collapses into a 3-minute buy-everything spree followed by 20–44 minutes with a single new rung and nothing money-priced in the 'save for it' band. That is one real, measurable gameplay flaw (contractPass=false) in an otherwise polished module, so it scores 7.5 and fails the ≥8.5 gate; the fix is structural (more earnings-gated rungs between 1e10 and 1e14 with a lower gate share), not a knob.
issues: [high] Purchase tension 24% vs the ≥30% contract (logs/sim-gauntlet.json issues[0]; contractPass=false). Concretely, after city 1 each replay is a ~3-minute seed spree that buys the whole core ladder, then 20–44 minutes in which exactly ONE never-owned rung appears (cycles 4–30 newItems length = 0 or 1; cycles 12–30 average 27 min each). Samples show tensionNext ≈1.02–2.1 (cheapest unowned upgrade is instantly affordable) while tension (priciest) reads 4e3–5e8× cash — the money ladder in a replay city is either 'buy now' or 'hopeless', never 'save for it'. The core ladder ends at planetary-charter $7.8e9 (config) while late income is 1e12–1e15/s, so nothing money-priced sits in the 30 s–15 min band for hours. → Add 5–6 intermediate money rungs between 1e10 and 1e14 (×3–5 apart) with earnedGate so they open mid-city instead of at the seed spree, e.g. in src/upgrades/data.js FRONTIER add 'orbital-shipyard' 1e11 (all jobs +75%), 'terraforming-guild' 5e11 (housing +100%), 'antimatter-refinery' 3e12 (industry +150%), 'exchange-ring' 1.5e13 (commerce +150%); and lower FRONTIER_GATE from 0.25 to ~0.08 so a rung unlocks when it is still ~10× cash (≈2–10 min of income at the bot's growth rate) rather than ~4× total-earned. Re-run npm run sim -- --ticks 432000 and check metrics.tensionShare ≥ 0.30 and tensionNextShare rises off 0.07.

[medium] Cycle 4 (6.6 min) introduces zero new items (cycles[4].newItems=[]) and cycles 2–3 add only 2 and 1 — the hour between founding 1 and founding 5 is the weakest stretch: the player owns everything by minute 3 of each city and then watches income. Contract only guards foundings after the 5th, but the player feels it. → Put a rung in every one of cycles 2–5: retune charter-grid to unlock at legacy ≥ 10 / cost ◆14 (config 'charter-grid') so it lands in cycle 4, and add a cheap Legacy-category rung unlocked at hasLegacy(20) (e.g. 'city-archives': All jobs +50%, $2e7) so cycle 5 has two targets.

[medium] Shipped frontier ladder is not the ×10 ladder the module documents. src/upgrades/data.js header says 'six fixed-dollar rungs ×10 apart from $1e13 to $1e18' and 'the literals here match config', but src/balance/config.js ships dyson-swarm 1.8e10, quantum-exchange 5.2e11, mass-driver-port 6.5e13, ringworld-district 3.6e14, stellar-engine 5.6e14, galactic-charter 1.2e15 (ratios ×29, ×125, ×5.5, ×1.6, ×2.1) and planetary-charter 7.8e9 vs data 3e12. Ringworld→Stellar→Galactic are 1.6×/2.1× apart, so three top-tier rungs arrive in three consecutive cycles with one bought per cycle — the 'frontier' reads as a checklist rather than escalating goals, and the module's own docs/tests describe a ladder that never ships. → Either move the shipped spacing into data.js defaults (so the file is truthful) or enforce a minimum ×3 spacing in config: e.g. ringworld 3e14, stellar 1.2e15, galactic 5e15; update the data.js header comment (lines 24–30) and DESIGN.md 'Module contracts → upgrades' to state that config owns prices and that the ×10 text is a default only.

[low] Two perks/rungs carry a half-effect that the file's own header admits is near-worthless late: charter-civic 'Happiness +10% and all jobs +50%' (◆1,958) and preventive-care/modern-curriculum '+10% happiness' — at h≈2.8 (final sample happiness=2.829) +0.1 happiness is ≈+3% income, so the desc reads as a bigger promise than delivered, and a ◆2k permanent perk is carried mostly by the jobs term. → For charter-civic replace happier(0.1) with global('growth', 1.5) and re-word desc 'All jobs +50% · population grows +50% faster'; keep the +10% happiness wording only on rungs that unlock while h < 1.2 (community-events, green-belts).

[low] Turbine Blades ($300, windmills ×2) and Coal Scrubbers ($12k, coal +50%) are dead effects once the grid is solar/nuclear (from ~minute 25 on) yet are re-granted forever by Institutional Memory, and Grid Substations' +25% power is the weakest rung in the ladder — the Legacy panel and owned-chip list grow with rungs that do nothing. → Give the two plant-specific rungs a floor that survives the tech change (e.g. Turbine Blades: 'Windmills ×2 power and all power +5%'), or bump grid-substations to +40%; optionally hide owned-and-inert rungs in src/ui/upgrades.js owned-chip list when the building count is 0.

simulation.verdict: The simulation core is premium-quality code: allocation-free 0.008 ms ticks, NaN-safe integration, an earnings-only prestige rule that meets every structural point of the Late-game contract (no wall-clock gates, legacy as a spendable currency on the full bank, all 14 derived.extra.prestige fields, correct event payloads), and tests pass with zero attributable errors. It falls short of 8.5 because the shipped loop still fails the binding cadence contract in the 12 h sim (tension 24% vs >= 30%, 29-44 min late plateaus with one new item per founding, cycle 7 only passing the 1.35x rule via tolerance) and the module's own headers/DEFAULTS quote a previous tuning. Fix the tension target (extra mid-run rungs or lower minGainShare), refresh the docs and sync DEFAULTS, and this passes.
issues: [major] 12 h sim contract fails (logs/sim-gauntlet.json contractPass=false): purchase tension share 24% (reach) / 19% (ratio) vs the >= 30% the DESIGN.md contract requires. From founding ~12 onward cycles are 29-44 min plateaus (cycle 18 = 44.5 min) in which each founding introduces exactly 1 never-bought item, so the loop is a near-flat earn-to-threshold wait with no visible mid-run target. Cycle 7 (9.7 -> 13.57 min, x1.40) clears the 1.35x cadence rule only via the +0.5 min tolerance in tools/economy-sim.mjs:185. → Owned jointly with balance/upgrades, but the simulation side can supply targets: (a) add an in-run legacy milestone rung between foundings (e.g. milestones.js 'legacy-N' ladder x2 instead of x2.5-3.3, or per-run money milestones between 1e13 and 1e17 spaced x3) so a rung is always 30 s-15 min away; (b) lower config.prestige.minGainShare from 0.4 to ~0.3 so late cycles shorten to 15-25 min; re-run npm run sim -- --ticks 432000 until tensionShare >= 0.30 and every cycle ratio <= 1.35 without the 0.5 min slack.

[minor] src/simulation/prestige.js header 'Measured' paragraph is stale: it quotes the 2026-09-04 tree (threshold $3M, Found arms at $3M, 17 foundings, legacy 380, exponent 0.35 arithmetic) while shipped config.prestige is threshold 9.24e6 / exponent 0.488 / minGainShare 0.4 and the gauntlet shows 31 foundings and legacy 193k. The contract line for *simulation* explicitly requires 'refreshed header docs with measured numbers'. index.js header also claims 0.02-0.03 ms/tick and ~22k t/s vs measured 0.008 ms and 48k t/s. → Replace the prestige.js 'Measured' paragraph with the logs/sim-gauntlet.json figures (first founding 41.5 min, cycles 16/17.6/5.4/6.6..., 31 foundings, legacy 193,474, money peak 8.4e16) and the shipped knobs; update the index.js timing sentence.

[minor] src/simulation/tuning.js DEFAULTS.prestige (threshold 3e6, exponent 0.35, incomePerLegacy 0.04, legacyPower 0.5, firstBonus 0.3, minGainShare 0.05) no longer match src/balance/config.js (9.24e6, 0.488, 0.01, 0.6, 0.23, 0.4). A missing/malformed config section silently runs a completely different economy. resources/index.js enforces DEFAULTS == config in its tests; simulation does not. → Sync DEFAULTS.prestige to the shipped values and add a drift test in simulation.test.mjs asserting DEFAULTS.prestige deep-equals config.prestige (mirroring resources.test.mjs), or import the shipped block as the fallback.

[minor] src/simulation/index.js simulate(): prestigeStatus() runs after checkMilestones(), so the 'founding-charter' milestone (milestones.js canFound reads derived.extra.prestige.can) and its progress bar see the previous tick's snapshot; on load/prestige the first tick evaluates against the pre-reset snapshot from recompute(). → Call prestigeStatus(state, ensurePrestigeExtra(derived), config) immediately after integrate() and before checkMilestones()/checkGates(), so every milestone/gate reads this tick's figures.

[minor] tap(): gain = max($1, grossIncome x tapSeconds) with tapSeconds = 1, and nothing in the module (upgrades, milestones, legacy) ever scales tapSeconds or references stats.clicks. After the first minute a tap is worth one second of income, so the active-play verb has no progression hook, unlike Cookie Clicker's click-upgrade ladder. → Expose a mods.tap multiplier (add to createMods/sanitizeMods and read it in tap()) and give at least one milestone/perk a tap reward (e.g. 'clicks-100' milestone: x5 tap value; a charter perk: taps pay 30 s of income) so tapping has a reason to exist past minute 1.

ui.verdict: PASS. The UI is premium-indie quality: a disciplined frame loop (change-guarded DOM writes, ~0.6-1.0 ms/frame, 60 fps, zero errors at 1440 and 1100), a dashboard that visibly grows from an empty plot to a full city with a genuinely good SVG skyline, and the Charter perks section verified live inside the Legacy panel with the ◆ cost chips and available/total bank after the bot founded. Accessibility fundamentals (real buttons, focus-visible, modal focus trap, inline confirms, reduced motion) are all present. What keeps it from 9: toasts stacking over the Legacy panel's 'Found a new city' and 'Sign' buttons, the Employed/Unemployment tile contradiction, and small polish items ('-$0/s', truncated upgrade copy at 1100px, buy-button accessible names, Legacy-vs-Charter naming overlap).
issues: [medium] Toasts are sticky to the bottom of the hero column and stack over the Legacy panel: in shot-1100-founded.png two toasts sit directly on the 'Found a new city' button and the Charter 'Sign' cards, and at 1440 (shot-1440-founded.png) they cover the charter card. Milestone/unlock bursts are frequent and hovering pauses the timer, so the prestige CTA is repeatedly blocked exactly when it matters. → In styles.css .toasts (line 2119) anchor the host to the top of the hero scrollport instead: position: sticky; top: 0; order: -1; and .toast-stack { top: 6px; bottom: auto } so toasts overlay the skyline (a large forgiving tap target) rather than the Legacy panel's buttons; alternatively drop MAX_VISIBLE in src/ui/toast.js to 1 while .panel-prestige is visible.

[medium] City Stats tiles contradict each other: 'Employed 45 / 45' sits next to 'Unemployment 80.0%' (shot-1440-40.png). The first tile is employed/jobs, but its label reads as 100% employment. → In src/ui/hero.js line 156 rename statRow('employed', 'Employed') to 'Jobs filled' (or render `${emp} of ${workers} working`) so the pair reads coherently.

[low] Buy buttons have no per-building accessible name; screen readers hear 'Buy $218' with no building (src/ui/build.js card() line 156). → In updateCard (build.js line 288) add setAttr(c.btn, 'aria-label', `${label} ${def.name} for ${money(cost)}`) alongside the label/cost writes.

[low] Upkeep tile prints '-$0/s' when upkeep is zero (visible in every gauntlet screenshot), which reads like a formatting bug. → src/ui/hero.js line 308: guard zero -> setText(statEls.upkeep, br.upkeep > 0 ? '-$' + short(br.upkeep) + '/s' : '$0/s').

[low] At 1100px the 300px side column truncates upgrade descriptions with ellipsis ('Malls earn +100% income and provi...', 'Dynasty Ledger ... x6 at...') and wraps names onto two lines, so the formula-style Legacy upgrades lose their payoff text (shot-1100-founded.png, shot2-1100-legacy-scrolled.png). → styles.css: inside @media (max-width: 1180px) reduce .ucard-buy width from 86px to 76px and .ucard padding to 8px, and raise .ucard-desc -webkit-line-clamp to 3 in that range; or make .ucard-cat inline with the name at narrow widths.

[low] Two pink 'legacy' concepts coexist: money-priced upgrades labelled 'LEGACY' in the Upgrades panel ($5,000 Legacy Archive) and legacy-priced 'Charter' perks in the Legacy panel, both using --c-prestige. A player seeing 'LEGACY ... Buy $5,000' next to 'Charter ... Sign ◆ 8' has to learn the distinction from the currency glyph alone. → src/ui/content.js EXTRA_CATEGORIES: rename the money-priced category to 'Heritage' or 'Legacy-tier' and give it a distinct accent (e.g. #e879f9) so only ◆-priced items carry the prestige pink.

[low] Early/mid game the center build column is >50% empty (only 2-3 cards per category) while the side column overflows (scrollHeight 1458-1800 vs 804 visible), so Milestones and the City Log sit below the fold at 1440 (screenshot-gauntlet-mid.png). → Show two locked teaser cards instead of one in build.js rebuild() line 394 (items.filter(!unlocked).slice(0,2)), and at >=1240px move .panel-log into the build column footer so the center column carries live information.

[low] reducedMotion in src/ui/dom.js line 94 is sampled once at module load; toggling the OS setting mid-session leaves JS tweens/particles animating until reload. → Expose a getter backed by matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') with an addEventListener('change') handler, and have callers read it at use time.

save.verdict: PASS. src/save/index.js is a genuinely hardened persistence layer: 12 hostile payloads, blocked storage, quota errors, 2h and 10h offline returns, export/import and hard reset all behaved correctly in real Chrome with zero console errors, and the offline catch-up keeps the frame gap under 50ms while honoring a consistent 50% efficiency on both the simulated and analytic paths. What keeps it below 9 are polish items rather than reliability defects: offline ticks inflate the visible playtime clock, background-tab catch-up silently applies the offline penalty, the migration runner has never been exercised by a test, and a parked corrupt save has no recovery UI.
issues: [minor] Offline catch-up inflates stats.playtime: stepScaled() calls game.step(n) and core/loop.js tick() adds DT to state.stats.playtime per tick, so after 10 min played + 2h away the topbar clock (src/ui/topbar.js:95) shows '2h 10m' and the Stats modal 'Playtime' is wrong. Visible in offline-toast.png. → In stepScaled() (src/save/index.js) capture const play0 = state.stats.playtime before game.step(n) and restore state.stats.playtime = play0 afterwards (optionally add stats.offlineTime += n * DT so the time is still accounted for).

[minor] Migration path is unexercised and untested: MIGRATIONS = {} and no tool imports parseSave/runMigrations, so the first real STATE_VERSION bump will ship the first-ever run of that code. → Add tools/save-test.mjs (Node, no DOM) that imports parseSave from src/save/index.js and asserts fixtures: a v1 envelope, an unversioned bare state, a v(N+1) state, and a stalled-migration state keep the expected version; wire it into package.json 'verify'.

[minor] A save from a newer version keeps state.version=99 after best-effort load (runMigrations stamps st.version = v), and the next autosave writes envelope version 1 with inner state.version 99, so the '[save] save is from a newer version' warning repeats on every load forever. → In runMigrations() set st.version = Math.min(v, STATE_VERSION) after the loop, and have buildPayload() write version from STATE_VERSION only (it already does) so the inner value matches.

[minor] Background-tab catch-up (source 'background', via loop.skippedMs) uses the same 50% offlineEfficiency and, because finishCatchUp() gates only on seconds >= offlineMinSec (30s), pops the 'While you were away' toast after a 30s alt-tab. That is a stealth 50% income penalty for merely switching tabs, harsher than Cookie Clicker / Antimatter Dimensions. → In stepScaled()/finishCatchUp() use eff = catchUp.source === 'background' ? 1 : cfg.offlineEfficiency, and only emit the toast for source 'background' when seconds >= 300.

[nit] The corrupt copy parked under metropolis.save.v1.corrupt is never surfaced: src/ui/modal.js has no recovery affordance, so an unreadable save is a silent total loss for the player even though the bytes are kept. → registerAction('exportCorrupt', () => storage?.getItem(CORRUPT_KEY) || '') in src/save/index.js and show a 'Recover previous city' row in the settings modal when saveStatus() reports hasCorrupt: true.

[nit] coerceShape() accepts any finite integer: a save with tick=1e300 and buildings.house=1e300 loads (verified), after which state.tick++ no longer advances (1e300+1 === 1e300) and building counts exceed api.js MAX_COUNT (1e9). → In coerceShape() clamp st.tick to Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and each building count to 1e9 (the MAX_COUNT used by buy()).

[nit] 'Welcome back, Mayor. The city kept your seat warm.' is appended to state.log on every load, including a 3-second refresh, so the log fills with greetings. → In loadFromStorage() only addLog the welcome line when (Date.now() - r.savedAt) / 1000 >= cfg.offlineMinSec.

[high] Purchase-tension contract fails: cheapest unlocked-unowned money upgrade is 30 s-15 min of income away in only 24% of samples (reachShare 0.238, logs/sim-gauntlet.json metrics; reproduced on current tree), contract >= 30%. Cause is structural in config.upgrades: the 16 late core rungs (megastructures $2.1e9 ... galactic-charter $1.2e15) are placed one per city, so during the 10-35 minute plateau of every replay the cheapest unowned upgrade is the NEXT city's rung at >50x cash (hopeless), while everything else is instant. → Add repeatable in-cycle content in config.upgrades: a money-priced 'Municipal Bonds' ladder whose cost = max(1e6, 240 s of current income) x1.5 per purchase, +4% income each, up to ~8 per city and reset on founding. That puts a 4-10 minute target on the card for the whole plateau without moving the cycle table. Re-run npm run sim -- --ticks 432000 and require reachShare >= 0.30.

[high] Dead late-game plateaus vs the Cookie Clicker bar. From the per-city sample table: cities 8-28 gain 0-1 upgrades after minute 3 of the replay and spend 10-35 minutes at <1%/min income growth (city 17: 35 min, 0 new upgrades, 25 flat minutes; city 18: 44.5 min, 1 upgrade, 34 flat minutes; city 28: 41.6 min, 35 flat minutes). Income over the plateau grows only x1.16-1.4 while the player buys ~200 buildings each adding <0.5%. That is a 30-45 minute wait for the Found button in hours 4-8 and 10-11. → Same bond ladder as above plus building-count milestones per type (25/50/100 owned -> +5% income each, config.milestones) so the 200 building buys per cycle carry visible steps. For city 18 specifically, price quantum-exchange 5.2e11 -> 3.5e11 so the x2.8 rung lands in the first half of city 18 instead of lifting only city 19.

[medium] The visible 'next big thing' is hopeless from minute 28 on. config.upgrades prices core rungs at 1e9-1e14 while src/upgrades/data.js still unlocks them on building/pop counts: megastructures ($2.1e9, unlock 3 arcologies) appears at 28 min of city 1 when cash is $1.2e5 and income $28k/s (17,900x cash, 21 h of income); arcology-gardens ($7.6e12) at 32 min; superconductor-grid ($9.1e13) at 35 min = 5e8x cash. Sample bigRatio stays 4e3-6e5 through hours 2-6 (7 h to 14 days of income). Contract text calls this 'hopeless'; Cookie Clicker keeps the priciest visible item at 3-50x. → Give every late core rung an earnings gate like the frontier: in config.upgrades add unlockAt: { earned: cost/4 } (or an earnedGate: 0.25 field consumed by the same applyOverride -> frontierUnlock path), so a rung shows up when the run has earned a quarter of its price. Keep the count/pop rule as an AND if the flavour matters.

[medium] Saver profile breaches both magnitude ceilings: npm run sim -- --saver --ticks 432000 reports money peak 1.96e18 (> 1e18) and legacy 1,459,373 (> 1e6), 37 foundings, 13 empty late cycles (logs/sim-saver.json, reproduced). DESIGN.md: 'both profiles must stay free of overflow/stall/magnitude issues'. → Retune with both profiles in the loop: prestige.exponent 0.488 -> ~0.47 (legacy at 12 h drops ~35%) with firstBonus nudged up (~0.26-0.27) so the default profile's 30th founding stays in hour 12; add two charter perks above Imperial (2e5, 5e5 legacy) as sinks so a saver's surplus has a target. Gate contractPass on the saver run's magnitude issue as well.

[low] Cadence ratio misses: cycle 7 (9.7 -> 13.57 min, x1.40), cycle 9 (16.53 -> 22.4, x1.36) and cycle 28 (30.6 -> 41.57, x1.36) exceed the contract's 'each cycle <= 1.35x the previous'. They pass only because tools/economy-sim.mjs:185 adds +0.5 min slack that the DESIGN.md contract text does not grant. → Either write the +0.5 min slack into DESIGN.md's cadence line, or strengthen the rungs entering those cities: Standing Orders (city 7) gets +10% income, and charter-energy (city 28, no replay income effect) gets a +15% income clause so the Energy Charter city is not the x1.36 step.

[low] Civic 'matters' only by the letter: all 19 happiness dips are the replay's first-minute spree (cycles[].minHappiness 0.36/0.51 in the opening seconds, happiness 2.1-2.8 thereafter); no mature city ever dips, so parks/schools never bind after city 1. → Raise happiness.pollutionScale 0.35 -> 0.45 or let the legacy clean-air tiers scale slower, so a refinery-heavy replay drifts under 1.0 mid-city unless civic buildings keep coming; verify happinessDipCities stays >= 50% and the dips occur after runMin 3.
